title: Gate deploy-play-store.yml on a passing CI run for the exact SHA being deployed
why: deploy-play-store.yml has no `needs:`/`workflow_run:` dependency on ci.yml and no step that checks the target SHA's check-run status. Its only steps between checkout and Play Store upload are checkout, codegen, and `flutter build appbundle --release` — no `flutter test`, `dart analyze`, `make audit`, or firestore-rules check. A maintainer who tags a commit that never went through review/CI (an emergency hotfix, a stale local branch, the wrong SHA) or whose ci.yml run is still red/in-progress can ship straight to Google Play production with nothing in the committed config to stop it — the only backstop is human diligence, which is exactly the kind of implicit, non-deterministic gate Rule 0 says not to rely on.
recommendation: Add a job that queries the GitHub Checks API for the deploying SHA's required workflows before the build/upload steps run (or trigger deploys via a `workflow_call` from a successful ci.yml run instead of independent `push: tags`/`workflow_dispatch` triggers).
acceptance_criteria: deploy-play-store.yml fails fast if the deploying SHA has no green ci.yml run, before any build/signing steps execute.
A dry run against a SHA with a failing/missing CI run demonstrates the new gate blocking the deploy.
